title: Jude and the Postcards
premise: Theo 'Jude' Galloway, a celebrated restaurant critic who lost her sense of taste after her brother's death, has spent three years writing reviews that say everything except what she means. When a song she wrote at nineteen — never recorded, given away in a letter — plays on a late-night radio show credited to a stranger named Jude, she follows it to a coastal town where her family's old boarding house is scheduled for demolition in six weeks. Among the postcards her brother mailed from every place he never lived, she uncovers the truth of what he gave up for her and why she stopped tasting anything the day he left. To save the house, she must publicly confess the review that destroyed a young chef's career — justice the law never demanded but conscience does — and forgive both the stranger in the photographs and herself. The novel ends on demolition day: the house falls, but Jude tastes salt air for the first time in three years, and the chef's new restaurant opens where the garden stood.
about_author: Felix Hartwell is the pen name of a former line cook who spent a decade writing obituaries for small-town newspapers before turning to fiction. He lives near the sea, collects unsent letters, and believes most stories are apologies that arrived too late.

chapters.title: The Art of Almost
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A lavish tasting menu at an acclaimed restaurant; Jude writes a glowing review that says nothing true, unable to taste any of it. Her editor praises its 'restraint.' Emotional beat: hollow competence masking grief.

chapters.title: Static on the Late Shift
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Driving home at 2 a.m., a radio station plays a song she wrote at nineteen and never recorded. The host credits 'Jude.' She pulls over, shaking. Beat: the past reaching through the wire.

chapters.title: Postcards from Nowhere
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. In her apartment she opens the shoebox of postcards her brother Danny mailed from towns he claimed to live in — all addressed to a house she thought was sold. Beat: suspicion kindled into purpose.

chapters.title: The Address That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. She traces the return address to Salt Hollow, a fading coastal town, and learns the boarding house there is still standing — with a demolition notice dated six weeks out. Beat: dread and pull in equal measure.

chapters.title: Room Seven
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, arriving in Salt Hollow. She checks into the crumbling boarding house under a false name; the landlady, Marisol, seems to recognize something in her face. Beat: displacement, first breath of the town.

chapters.title: The Man Who Plays Other People's Songs
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. She watches the new guest and remembers the young man who left a tape labeled 'for whoever needs it' fifteen years ago. Beat: keeper-of-secrets tenderness.

chapters.title: Photographs of a Stranger
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. In the house's hallway she finds framed photos: Danny, laughing, embedded in town life she never knew — a life that ran parallel to hers. Beat: betrayal's first sting.

chapters.title: The Chef Who Lost Everything
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus Okafor, the chef Jude's infamous early review ruined, now runs a food truck at the edge of town, feeding dockworkers. He doesn't know who she is. Beat: quiet dignity over old wounds.

chapters.title: A Meal She Can't Taste
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Cyrus serves her without knowing her; the food is extraordinary and she feels nothing. She lies to his face about how good it is. Beat: shame sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Demolition Date
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. At the town office she discovers the demolition petition was filed by a developer — and co-signed by a name she knows: her mother's. Beat: the ground tilts.

chapters.title: Letters Never Sent
chapters.summary: Danny's POV, flashback. Fifteen years earlier: Danny writes the letter enclosing the song, deciding to give up music and take the blame for something that wasn't his. Beat: sacrificial love turning to erasure.

chapters.title: What Mother Signed
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A phone call home goes badly; her mother deflects, then hangs up. Jude finds the mother's signature on documents selling the house's land twice over. Beat: familial betrayal made concrete.

chapters.title: The Radio Man
chapters.summary: Deacon's POV. Deacon, the late-night DJ, found the tape in a donation box and built a small cult following around 'the mystery of Jude.' He's coming to Salt Hollow to find the songwriter. Beat: innocent catalyst in motion.

chapters.title: Town Meeting
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The town votes on whether to fight the demolition; old grudges surface, including resentment toward the boarding house's 'outsider history.' Jude speaks and is nearly unmasked. Beat: community as contested ground.

chapters.title: Cyrus Remembers the Review
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. A customer mentions the famous critic is in town; Cyrus realizes the woman in his truck is Jude Galloway. He says nothing. Beat: the trap of withheld truth.

chapters.title: Room Seven at Night
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Insomnia; she reads Danny's postcards properly for the first time and realizes each describes a meal — he was writing her the taste she'd lost. Beat: grief reframed as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Garden Wall
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol shows Jude the walled garden behind the house where Danny taught local kids songs; she reveals Danny paid the house's debts anonymously for years. Beat: the brother larger than memory.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Truck
chapters.summary: Two-hander, Jude and Cyrus. Jude confesses who she is mid-meal. Cyrus hands her the printed review he's kept laminated for ten years. Beat: collision, no absolution offered.

chapters.title: What the Review Didn't Say
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Flashback to the night after the review ran: the restaurant closing, his marriage fraying, the dish he never got to serve. Beat: cost itemized.

chapters.title: Deacon Arrives
chapters.summary: Deacon's POV. The DJ rolls into town broadcasting live, playing the song on loop, drawing crowds and the developer's lawyers. Beat: pressure cooker sealed.

chapters.title: The Developer's Offer
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The developer offers Jude money to walk away — revealing he knows exactly who she is, and that her mother sold him the story. Beat: temptation wearing a familiar face.

chapters.title: Mother Comes to Town
chapters.summary: Two-hander, Jude and her mother. Her mother arrives to stop her, and finally admits Danny took the fall for her father's fraud — and that she signed the demolition to bury it. Beat: the wound named aloud.

chapters.title: The Song's Second Verse
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Deacon plays an alternate take of the song — one with lyrics only Danny would know, addressed to Jude by name. She realizes the tape was always meant to find her. Beat: devastation transfigured into summons.

chapters.title: Salt Hollow Remembers
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter. Townspeople begin leaving offerings at the garden wall — recipes, lyrics, memories of Danny. The demolition becomes a town cause. Beat: belonging arriving uninvited.

chapters.title: Cooking Without a Kitchen
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus, moved despite himself, cooks on the beach for the town using the boarding house's abandoned garden produce. Jude helps and almost tastes something. Beat: thaw, one degree.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Legal challenge to the demolition fails on procedure; justice inside the law proves unavailable. Marisol's hand on her shoulder. Beat: the law closes its door.

chapters.title: Confession Drafted
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude writes a public retraction of the decade-old review, naming herself, her methods, and her cruelty — and can't decide whether publishing it saves or destroys Cyrus again. Beat: ethics of atonement.

chapters.title: Cyrus's Answer
chapters.summary: Two-hander. Jude shows Cyrus the draft. He reads it twice and says: publish it, but only if you also cook something true. Beat: forgiveness conditioned on courage.

chapters.title: The Meal
chapters.summary: Alternating Jude/Cyrus POV. In the boarding house kitchen, Cyrus guides Jude through cooking Danny's favorite dish from the postcards. Midway, taste returns — salt, fat, grief, sweetness. Beat: climax of the inner arc.

chapters.title: Publication
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The confession runs nationally; her career detonates, her editor calls it suicide, her mother stops speaking to her. Jude feels lighter than she has in years. Beat: consequence embraced.

chapters.title: The Developer Escalates
chapters.summary: Villain-adjacent POV. The developer moves the demolition up two weeks and files harassment claims against Deacon's broadcast. Beat: vise tightening.

chapters.title: Occupying the Garden
chapters.summary: Ensemble. The town physically occupies the garden wall; Cyrus feeds them; Marisol reads Danny's postcards aloud over Deacon's radio. Beat: solidarity as resistance.

chapters.title: The Photographs Explained
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol reveals the final secret: the photographs were sent by Danny himself, so someone would remember him whole if he never came back. Jude forgives the stranger in them. Beat: forgiveness achieved.

chapters.title: Demolition Eve
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Night before the bulldozers. Jude sleeps in Room Seven, the song playing from every window in town, and writes Danny a postcard of her own. Beat: stillness before rupture.

chapters.title: Demolition Day
chapters.summary: Ensemble climax. As machines arrive, Deacon broadcasts the song's origin story nationwide; the developer, exposed by the fraud documents Jude publishes, withdraws under legal threat — but the east wing falls anyway. Beat: victory and loss entangled.

chapters.title: What Stands
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Surveying the ruin, the town proposes rebuilding the garden as a public kitchen. Cyrus asks Jude, not the critic, what should grow there. Beat: identity remade.

chapters.title: The New Restaurant
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus signs the lease for a small restaurant on the old footprint, named Postcards. He offers Jude the job of writing the menu's stories — honestly this time. Beat: vocation reborn.

chapters.title: Reconciliation, Partial
chapters.summary: Two-hander, Jude and her mother. Her mother comes to the garden, not to apologize fully but to plant something. It isn't complete forgiveness; it's a beginning. Beat: imperfect grace.

chapters.title: First Service
chapters.summary: Ensemble. Opening night at Postcards: Deacon broadcasts live, Marisol hosts, the town fills the tables. Jude tastes every course and cries into the soup. Beat: fullness.

chapters.title: Postscript: A Postcard Returned
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, coda. Months later, a postcard arrives with no sender — Danny's handwriting, a line from the song, postmarked the week he died. Jude pins it above the kitchen door and gets back to work. Beat: love that outlasts explanation.
